Chip Supply Chain · Chapter 02 · Stage 2 of 15

Silicon and Wafers

Every chip starts as a wafer: a mirror-polished disc of silicon 300 millimetres across. A furnace melts purified sand, and a machine pulls a cylinder out of the melt the way a candle is dipped, except that what comes out is a single crystal, every atom on the same repeating grid. Saws slice that cylinder into discs, polished until nothing on the surface stands more than a few atoms proud. Fewer than one atom in a hundred billion may be anything but silicon, and the flatness has to hold right to the edge. Only five firms can do it reliably, and none of them is American or Chinese.
